reasons: Only the owner's blocks are checked when joining.

terms.meaning: the member who controls a crew and can remove members or change its code
random values hard to predict, suitable for codes that act as keys

sections.name: File setup, newInviteCode
sections.title: Imports and invite code maker
sections.what: Brings in the random number source, error types, the public user shape and the repository. Builds six character invite codes from letters and digits, leaving out look-alike characters such as O and 0.
sections.why: Likely reason: secure randomness makes codes hard to guess, and leaving out look-alikes helps people type them.

sections.name: requireMembership
sections.title: Membership gate
sections.what: Stops the request unless the user is in the crew. Non-members get a not-found error, so outsiders cannot tell a crew exists.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps crew existence private, as the comment states.

sections.name: getCrewForMember
sections.title: Full crew view for a member
sections.what: Returns a crew's details and member list for a member. Members the viewer has blocked stay in the list but show a generic name and no picture.
sections.why: Likely reason: blocked people remain in shared crews, but the blocker should not see their names.
sections.watch_out: The invite code is included, so every member can see it.

sections.name: listMyCrews
sections.title: Crews a user is in
sections.what: Returns a summary of each crew for the user, with the member count and whether the user owns it.
sections.why: Likely reason: builds the crew list page.

sections.name: memberIds
sections.title: Member ID list
sections.what: Confirms the caller is a member, then returns all member IDs for the crew.
sections.why: Likely reason: a guarded lookup so non-members cannot list members.

sections.name: withFreshCode
sections.title: Retry for invite code clash
sections.what: Tries to make and save an invite code up to five times, retrying only when the database reports a duplicate.
sections.why: Likely reason: random codes can rarely clash, and the retry handles it.

sections.name: createCrew
sections.title: Creating a crew
sections.what: Creates a crew with a fresh invite code and makes the caller its owner.
sections.why: Likely reason: each new crew gets its own code straight away.

sections.name: requireOwner
sections.title: Owner only check
sections.what: Confirms the caller is a member and the owner of the crew, and otherwise refuses with a not-found or forbidden error.
sections.why: Likely reason: several actions are for owners only, and this keeps that check in one place.

sections.name: leaveCrew
sections.title: Leaving a crew
sections.what: Lets a member leave. An owner may leave only if they are the last member, in which case the crew is deleted.
sections.why: Likely reason: prevents a crew from being left with no owner.
sections.watch_out: An owner who is the last member leaving deletes the crew, and that cannot be undone.

sections.name: removeMember
sections.title: Owner removes a member
sections.what: Lets the owner remove another member. The owner cannot remove themselves, and the target must be in the crew.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops an owner removing themselves and leaving the crew without one.

sections.name: rotateInviteCode
sections.title: Owner resets invite code
sections.what: Lets the owner replace the crew's invite code, so old codes and links stop working.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets an owner shut out people who hold an old link.

sections.name: transferOwnership
sections.title: Owner hands over the crew
sections.what: Lets the owner make another current member the owner.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a crew carry on when its owner steps back.

sections.name: joinCrew
sections.title: Joining with a code
sections.what: Finds the crew by invite code and adds the user as a member. A wrong code, or a block by the owner, gives the same not-found message.
sections.why: Likely reason: a blocked person gets the same reply as a wrong code, so they cannot tell they are blocked.
sections.watch_out: Only the owner's blocks are checked, so a block by another member does not stop someone joining.

sections.name: joinOrOpen
sections.title: Join or open from a link
sections.what: Used by invite links. If the user is already in the crew, it returns the crew without joining. If a race makes the join fail with a conflict, it also returns the crew.
sections.why: Likely reason: a link opened twice, for example by a prefetch, should not show an error.
sections.watch_out: The joined flag says whether a new join happened, so callers must check it, not just the ID.

summary: Crew rules: creating, joining by code or link, leaving, owner actions, and member views.
purpose: The rules behind every crew feature.
why: Likely reason: the header says checks sit here so every page and API that uses this service is protected.
how: 1. Check membership or ownership. 2. Apply the action. 3. Return results or raise a clear error. Invite codes are made from secure random numbers, with up to five retries on a clash.
inputs: A user ID, a crew ID, names, invite codes, and target user IDs.
outputs: Crew details, summaries, IDs, new invite codes, or errors.
risks: Only the owner's blocks decide who can join. Members can see the invite code. An owner who leaves a one-person crew deletes it.
debug: Not found hides non-members. Conflict means the user is already in the crew. Forbidden means the caller is not the owner.
